scope: The thinker cards on the reading route: Aristotle, Spinoza, Nietzsche, Deleuze, Guattari, Land; added 2026-11-03: Bergson, Bataille; added 2026-11-21: Hume

by.review: Independent reviewer (Claude subagent, fresh context), 2026-10-24, 25 searches and fetches: Aristotle and Spinoza pass; Nietzsche, Deleuze, Guattari and Land pass after fixes now made (the archived Wicks entry added as a source; a repeated sentence on Deleuze's illness; the Guattari source credited to Adam Shatz; Land's move to Shanghai dated loosely, his essay named, and an unquoted run from Burrows reworded). Guattari's analysis with Lacan is left undated, as sources disagree (Britannica: the 1950s; Universalis: until 1960; other accounts 1962–69).
by.review_2026_11_03: Independent reviewer (separate agent, fresh context), 2026-11-03: Bergson passes as drafted; Bataille passes after unconfirmed biographical details were cut and wording brought to Stoekl's.

note: Biographical claims were checked against the sources below; claims marked not-retrieved are the card's standard doctrine, which the cited Stanford entry covers but which was not re-read in this pass. Unsupported details were cut and errors corrected.

sources: Allan Stoekl, “Bataille, Georges (1897–1962)”, Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 2nd ed. (Macmillan, 2005), via encyclopedia.com

checked: 1897–1962 (Stoekl; Maskit); born in Billom, raised in Reims, much of his adult life in Paris; librarian at the Bibliothèque nationale 1922–1942 (Maskit)
'loosely associated with and against the surrealists' (Stoekl, verbatim)

Acéphale: secret society founded by Bataille in 1936, review published with Klossowski and Masson in June 1936; College of Sociology founded 1937 with Leiris and Caillois; Histoire de l'œil, Paris 1928, under the pseudonym Lord Auch (Morando, pp. 81, 83)
“The Notion of Expenditure”: Stoekl brackets it [1932], Piel 'l'article de 1933'; the card keeps 1933 in the works and '1932–33' in its text

general economy, 'the extravagant squandering of wealth', a person's 'fundamental tendency was to expend', 'the affirmation of life to the point of the risk of death', Mauss and the potlatch (Stoekl); restricted economy, squandering of energy, surplus destined for sacrifice, festivals, base materialism and cosmic expenditure, the sacred and the interdict, transgression and limits (Trebežnik)

Inner Experience 1943, the 'ecstatic horror' of God's definitive absence; Erotism 1957, erotic 'communication'; The Accursed Share 1949; at the vanguard of the French reception of Nietzsche and Hegel, 'following and rewriting Alexandre Kojève's Hegel'; Derrida's reading 'may be seen as the model of the deconstructive project'; Foucault's counter-discourse 'clearly owes much to Bataille' (Stoekl)
drew on Hegel, Nietzsche and Mauss (Maskit); Kojève (Stoekl)
fixed: École des Chartes (1918) and archivist-paleographer (1922) cut: found only in Larousse, which names no author
the review Documents (1929), Contre-Attaque with Breton and the founding of Critique (1946) cut: no academic source reached confirms them (Larousse and a university library's list only)
'He died in Paris' made 'He died in 1962'; 'in the Auvergne' replaced by Maskit's Billom, Reims and Paris
the Surrealists sentence given as Stoekl's words, in quotation marks
'part of the Summa Atheologica' and the sovereignty clause ('the moment freed from servitude to utility') cut: not in the sources reached
'the basic tendency of human beings, and of societies' made 'a person's fundamental tendency' (Stoekl); 'restricted economy of scarcity' made 'restricted economy'
'a principal figure in the French reception' made Stoekl's 'at the vanguard'; 'can be seen' made his 'may be seen'
Larousse (unsigned) replaced among the sources by Maskit (Routledge) and Morando (RACAR)
not_retrieved: the treatment of sacrifice and festival as the spending of the 'accursed share' is supported by Trebežnik's surplus 'destined for sacrifice'; the term itself not re-read in a source
